name: Debt To Family
overview: Scripture teaches that financial relationships, including debts within family, carry significant spiritual and practical implications. God’s blessing enables His people to lend rather than borrow, highlighting a position of provision and stewardship (Deuteronomy 15:6). The righteous are called to show mercy and fulfill their obligations, avoiding the wicked pattern of borrowing without repayment (Psalms 37:21). Proverbs emphasizes the responsibility to do good when it is within one’s power and warns that borrowing places one in servitude to the lender, underscoring the importance of wise labor and honest dealings in family financial matters (Proverbs 3:27; 13:11; 22:7). Ultimately, God is the maker of both rich and poor, reminding believers that all financial roles exist under His sovereign authority (Proverbs 22:2).
